title: Time Based Key Value Store
summary: Implement TimeMap with set(key, value, timestamp) and get(key, timestamp).

contractDetails.constraints: At most 200,000 calls after construction. Keys and values have 1–100 lowercase English letters or digits. Timestamps are integers in [1, 10,000,000], and set timestamps increase strictly across all keys. The judge sends rows ["set", key, value, timestamp] or ["get", key, timestamp], with timestamps encoded as decimal strings in the fixture. The callable methods receive integer timestamps. Return the get results in call order.

statement: Implement TimeMap with set(key, value, timestamp) and get(key, timestamp). Set stores a value at that time. Get returns the value from the latest already executed set for the same key at or before the requested time. Return an empty string if nothing qualifies.

examples.explanation: The query at 8 precedes the update at 9.
The first key is absent, and the second query is before the first write.

The judge sends rows ["set", key, value, timestamp] or ["get", key, timestamp], with timestamps encoded as decimal strings in the fixture. The callable methods receive integer timestamps. Return the get results in call order.
hints: Conceptual: Each key has its own history, and later writes always have greater timestamps.
Directional: Keep an append-only list of timestamp and value pairs per key.
Implementation: Binary-search for the first timestamp greater than the query. Use its predecessor, or return an empty string when there is no predecessor.
complexityAnalysis: With a hash map and growable arrays, set takes O(1) expected amortized time and get takes O(log k) time for k writes to that key. Storage is O(w) entries for w writes, plus the stored text.
